written: 2026-09-05, from the fixture sources, BEFORE any implementation (ADR-001 key-first)
invariant: The changed diff is input, not fetched context. A new file may cause EXTERNAL dependencies to be fetched, but the changed file itself must never be fetched merely because it is new — every one of its lines is already in front of the reviewer.
grounded_in: ADR-A005: 'The reviewer already receives the diff — condition C is diff PLUS bundle. Duplicating it would double-count tokens.' The own-file move was earned by Experiment 1's `upsertFromPlaid`, a sibling in a MODIFIED file that the diff did not show. A new file shows everything.

rows.expected_items: no same_file_symbol_absence and no same_file_reference for this file
rows.why: namespace, use block, class, LABEL, store(), audit() are all added lines. Fetching any of them returns the diff to the reviewer who already has it.

rows.case: external references from the new file
rows.expected_items: App\Models\Package surface FETCHED (it is off-diff); App\Support\Existing is ALSO changed by this diff, so it is a judgement call recorded below
rows.expected_diagnostics: Log::info settled as framework-known; Package::create and Package::where flagged unresolved (ADR-A016, unchanged)
rows.why: A new file may absolutely pull external context. Only its OWN content is barred.
rows.note: Existing.php is itself in this diff. The key does not require the tool to notice that — cross-file de-duplication is a different question and is NOT in M11's scope. Whatever v0.1.0 does for it must simply not change.

rows.expected_items: existing own-file behaviour UNCHANGED — the added extra() calls $this->helper(), whose body the diff does not show, so a same_file_reference fetch of helper() is correct and must survive
rows.why: This is Experiment 1's earned move. M11 must narrow the move to new files only, and this row proves it did not narrow further.
UnifiedDiffParser::membersIn filters on the .php extension. Record the existing behaviour; invent nothing.

rows.expected_items: ZERO. No same_file_symbol_absence whose reason names `php`.
rows.why: Root cause measured: the extractor tokenises '<?php ' . $regionText, and when the region itself begins with `<?php` the literal re-tokenises as `<`, `?`, T_STRING(php). The `?` then satisfies isClassNamePosition()'s nullable-type rule (`?Name`), so `php` is recorded as a class name the use block does not import.
rows.reachable_only_via: addedLines contains only `+` lines, so `<?php` can only be an added line when the file is new. D1 is therefore a strict subset of G3 — but the tokenisation is wrong on its own terms and is fixed at the token layer, not by relying on the G3 suppression.

rows.case: lexical noise inside the new file
rows.why: The class docblock names Package::create() and Log::warning(); a line comment names Existing::helper() and Package::where(); audit() contains the string literals 'Package::create' and 'Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log::info' and a Package::class constant. None is a reference.

rows.expected: bundle_version, schema, assertion kinds, premises, levers, provenance shape, ItemPriority bands and token accounting all UNCHANGED
rows.why: M11 narrows one move for one file state. Anything else moving is a defect.
